newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Duisenberg hopes to become ECB's first president.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg hopes to become ECB's first president.

text.p: Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg told Reuters Financial Television on Tuesday he hoped to become the first European Central Bank (ECB) president but did not assume he would automatically be chosen for the job.
"I don't expect it, but I hope it...in the European Parliament I was asked: 'Are you a candidate?' and I simply said: 'Yes'" he said in an RFTV interview.

Duisenberg is due to take over in July as head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) -- the Frankfurt-based forerunner of the ECB -- and is widely regarded as a strong candidate to become the ECB's first president.
France, however, is reported to be pressing for one of its own nationals to be appointed president of the ECB and oversee the launch of the euro -- Europe's single currency -- in 1999.

Duisenberg said nationality should not be a factor in the appointment, adding it was more important that the ECB president should have a good reputation in the world of finance and central banking as required by the Maastricht Treaty.

Asked what qualities he could bring to the job, Duisenberg cited his 16 years of experience as a central bank governor, five years as a minister of finance, four on the staff of the International Monetary Fund and three as a commercial banker.
